root_cause.text: The `smq_invalidate_mapping` function in the dm-cache-policy-smq was not protected by a lock, allowing concurrent invocations from multiple workers in passthrough mode to race on the allocated blocks counter and internal data structures, leading to data races and potential use-after-free.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `spin_lock_irqsave` and `spin_unlock_irqrestore` around the critical section (del_queue, h_remove, free_entry) in `smq_invalidate_mapping`. The CVE description states that "the policy invalidate_mapping operation is called simultaneously from multiple workers, thus it should be protected by a lock" and describes the resulting data races and use-after-free.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch adds `spin_lock_irqsave` and `spin_unlock_irqrestore` around the critical section (del_queue, h_remove, free_entry) in `smq_invalidate_mapping`. candidates.rationale: Retrieves entry from cache alloc without lock; race could lead to accessing stale or freed entry.
Checks allocated flag without synchronization; race could cause misreading or writing to freed entry.
Returns error based on unsynchronized check; part of critical section without locking.
Removes entry from queue without lock; concurrent access could corrupt queue or cause use-after-free.
Removes entry from hash table without lock; concurrent insertion/removal could corrupt data structure.
Frees entry without lock; concurrent use could lead to use-after-free or double free.
Returns success after unprotected operations; part of critical section.

vuln_statements.explanation: Retrieves entry from cache alloc without lock; concurrent invocations can access stale or freed entry, leading to data race.
Checks the allocated flag without synchronization; race condition can cause misreading or writing to freed entry.
Returns error based on unsynchronized check; part of the critical section executed without lock protection.
Removes entry from queue without lock; concurrent modifications can corrupt queue structure or cause use-after-free.
Removes entry from hash table without lock; concurrent insertions/removals can corrupt the hash table structure.
Frees entry without lock; concurrent use of the same entry by another thread can lead to use-after-free or double free.
Returns success after unprotected operations; this statement is part of the critical section that lacks synchronization, contributing to the race condition.
